<tbody id="S3.E5"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle y</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E5.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle=W_{\text{base}}x+\frac{\alpha}{r}\sum_{j=1}^{k}w_{j}\cdot\delta_{:,:,j,:}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>W</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mtext>base</mtext></msub><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mi>α</mi><mi>r</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo></mstyle><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>k</mi></msup><mi>w</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>δ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0em">:</mo><mo>,</mo><mo rspace="0em">:</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mo>:</mo></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=W_{\text{base}}x+\frac{\alpha}{r}\sum_{j=1}^{k}w_{j}\cdot\delta_{:,:,j,:}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{\mathcal{S}},B_{\mathcal{S}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{\mathcal{S}},B_{\mathcal{S}}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the gathered subsets of adapter factor matrices.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Weight Field</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The weight field <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{\theta}:\mathbb{R}^{d_{z}}\to\mathbb{R}^{L\times N_{b}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>z</mi></msub></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{\theta}:\mathbb{R}^{d_{z}}\to\mathbb{R}^{L\times N_{b}}</annotation></semantics></math> is a small neural network that maps a capability coordinate <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>z</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{z}}</annotation></semantics></math> to gating logits over the adapter bases for each of the <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> transformer layers. The architecture consists of a three-layer MLP with LayerNorm at the input and GELU activations:</p>
<table id="S3.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{\theta}(z)=W_{3}\cdot\text{GELU}(W_{2}\cdot\text{GELU}(W_{1}\cdot\text{LN}(z)))" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mtext>GELU</mtext></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mtext>GELU</mtext></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mtext>LN</mtext></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{\theta}(z)=W_{3}\cdot\text{GELU}(W_{2}\cdot\text{GELU}(W_{1}\cdot\text{LN}(z)))</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{1}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{h}\times d_{z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>z</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{1}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{h}\times d_{z}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{h}\times d_{h}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>h</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{h}\times d_{h}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{3}\in\mathbb{R}^{(L\cdot N_{b})\times d_{h}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>h</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{3}\in\mathbb{R}^{(L\cdot N_{b})\times d_{h}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{h}</annotation></semantics></math> is a hidden dimension (256 in our experiments). The output is reshaped to <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[B,L,N_{b}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>L</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[B,L,N_{b}]</annotation></semantics></math>, providing per-layer gating logits.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For each layer <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>, the top-<math id="S3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> bases are selected and their weights are computed via softmax over the selected logits:</p>
<table id="S3.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{\ell}=\text{top-}k(F_{\theta}(z)_{\ell}),\quad w_{b}=\frac{\exp(F_{\theta}(z)_{\ell,b})}{\sum_{b^{\prime}\in\mathcal{S}_{\ell}}\exp(F_{\theta}(z)_{\ell,b^{\prime}})},\quad b\in\mathcal{S}_{\ell}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>top-</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{\ell}=\text{top-}k(F_{\theta}(z)_{\ell}),\quad w_{b}=\frac{\exp(F_{\theta}(z)_{\ell,b})}{\sum_{b^{\prime}\in\mathcal{S}_{\ell}}\exp(F_{\theta}(z)_{\ell,b^{\prime}})},\quad b\in\mathcal{S}_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This design cleanly separates stored capacity from active computation. The total number of adapter bases <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{b}</annotation></semantics></math> determines how much conditional knowledge the system can hold, while <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> determines how much computation is spent per forward pass. Increasing <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{b}</annotation></semantics></math> adds capacity without increasing per-token cost.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Coordinate Dynamics</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The capability coordinate <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> must be set appropriately for each input. Rather than requiring external task labels or manual routing, we learn a recurrent dynamics module <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> that evolves <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> based on the model’s own hidden state representations:</p>
<table id="S3.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t+1}=\tanh(W_{p}\cdot\text{LN}(\text{GRU}(h_{t},z_{t})))" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>tanh</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mtext>LN</mtext></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mtext>GRU</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t+1}=\tanh(W_{p}\cdot\text{LN}(\text{GRU}(h_{t},z_{t})))</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is a summary of the backbone’s hidden states (mean-pooled over the sequence dimension from the final layer), GRU is a Gated Recurrent Unit <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cho et al., 2014</a>)</cite>, LN is LayerNorm, and <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{p}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{z}\times d_{z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>z</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{p}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{z}\times d_{z}}</annotation></semantics></math> is a learned projection. The <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tanh" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>tanh</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tanh</annotation></semantics></math> nonlinearity bounds <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-1,1]^{d_{z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>z</mi></msub></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-1,1]^{d_{z}}</annotation></semantics></math>, preventing coordinate drift.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In our implementation, the coordinate update operates at the sequence level using a two-pass strategy. On the first forward pass, the backbone processes the input with the initial coordinate <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{0}=\mathbf{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>𝟎</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{0}=\mathbf{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, producing hidden states that are used to update <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{0}\to z_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{0}\to z_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>. A second forward pass with <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> produces the final output. This two-pass approach avoids the complexity of per-token coordinate updates within the backbone’s forward pass. The hidden states used for the coordinate update are detached from the computation graph to prevent gradients from flowing back through the backbone.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.4 </span>Training Objective</h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The training loss combines four terms:</p>
<table id="S3.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{\text{NLL}}+\lambda_{\text{lock}}\cdot\mathcal{L}_{\text{lock}}+\lambda_{\text{sep}}\cdot\mathcal{L}_{\text{sep}}+\lambda_{\text{budget}}\cdot\mathcal{L}_{\text{budget}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>NLL</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>lock</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>lock</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>sep</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>sep</mtext></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>budget</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>budget</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{\text{NLL}}+\lambda_{\text{lock}}\cdot\mathcal{L}_{\text{lock}}+\lambda_{\text{sep}}\cdot\mathcal{L}_{\text{sep}}+\lambda_{\text{budget}}\cdot\mathcal{L}_{\text{budget}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The next-token prediction loss <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{NLL}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>NLL</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{NLL}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the standard cross-entropy loss over the vocabulary. This is the primary learning signal that shapes the adapter bases and trains the weight field and coordinate dynamics.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The lock loss <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{lock}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>lock</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{lock}}</annotation></semantics></math> enforces functional preservation of committed regions (detailed in Section <a href="#S3.SS5" title="3.5 Region Commitment and Functional Locking ‣ 3 Method ‣ Non-Interfering Weight Fields: Treating Model Parameters as a Continuously Extensible Function" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.5</span></a>). When no regions have been committed (e.g., during the first task), <math id="S3.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{lock}}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>lock</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{lock}}=0</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The separation loss <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{sep}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>sep</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{sep}}</annotation></semantics></math> encourages the current task’s coordinates to occupy regions distinct from previously committed regions:</p>
<table id="S3.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{sep}}=\mathbb{E}_{z\sim p_{\text{current}}}\left[\max\left(0,\tau_{A}+m-d_{M}(z,\mu_{A},\Sigma_{A})\right)^{2}\right]" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>sep</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mtext>current</mtext></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{sep}}=\mathbb{E}_{z\sim p_{\text{current}}}\left[\max\left(0,\tau_{A}+m-d_{M}(z,\mu_{A},\Sigma_{A})\right)^{2}\right]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.p4.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{M}</annotation></semantics></math> is the Mahalanobis distance to the committed region with mean <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{A}</annotation></semantics></math> and covariance <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma_{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma_{A}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{A}</annotation></semantics></math> is the region threshold, and <math id="S3.SS4.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math> is an optional margin. This quadratic penalty activates only when coordinates fall within or too close to the committed region, pushing them outward without constraining where they end up.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The budget loss <math id="S3.SS4.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{budget}}=k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>budget</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{budget}}=k</annotation></semantics></math> is currently a constant since top-<math id="S3.SS4.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> is fixed, but it allows for future extensions with dynamic, input-dependent sparsity.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.5 </span>Region Commitment and Functional Locking</h3>

<div id="S3.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The commitment protocol is the mechanism that converts NIWF from a conditional adapter system into a continual learning framework with provable non-interference. After training on a task, the following procedure is executed.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">First, all training examples are passed through the model to collect the set of capability coordinates <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{z_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{z_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math> produced by the coordinate dynamics module. These coordinates represent the region of capability space that the task occupies.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Second, a Gaussian model is fit to the collected coordinates, yielding a mean <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>z</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{z}}</annotation></semantics></math> and covariance <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{z}\times d_{z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>z</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{z}\times d_{z}}</annotation></semantics></math>. The region boundary is defined using the Mahalanobis distance at the 95th percentile of the training distribution:</p>
<table id="S3.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}=\left\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{z}}:d_{M}(z,\mu,\Sigma)\leq\tau\right\},\quad\tau=Q_{0.95}\left(\{d_{M}(z_{i},\mu,\Sigma)\}_{i=1}^{N}\right)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>z</mi></msub></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mn>0.95</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}=\left\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{z}}:d_{M}(z,\mu,\Sigma)\leq\tau\right\},\quad\tau=Q_{0.95}\left(\{d_{M}(z_{i},\mu,\Sigma)\}_{i=1}^{N}\right)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS5.p3.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{0.95}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Q</mi><mn>0.95</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{0.95}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the 95th percentile.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Third, a set of anchor points <math id="S3.SS5.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{a_{j}\}_{j=1}^{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>M</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{a_{j}\}_{j=1}^{M}</annotation></semantics></math> is sampled from within <math id="S3.SS5.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}</annotation></semantics></math>, either by sampling from the fitted Gaussian and rejecting points outside the region, or by subsampling the empirical coordinate set. The field’s outputs on these anchors are recorded as the snapshot:</p>
<table id="S3.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E12.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="S_{j}=F_{\theta}(a_{j}),\quad j=1,\ldots,M" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{j}=F_{\theta}(a_{j}),\quad j=1,\ldots,M</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p5.1" class="ltx_p">During all subsequent training stages, the lock loss enforces that the field reproduces the same outputs on the anchors:</p>
<table id="S3.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{lock}}=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{j=1}^{M}\|F_{\theta}(a_{j})-S_{j}\|^{2}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>lock</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>M</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>M</mi></munderover><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{lock}}=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{j=1}^{M}\|F_{\theta}(a_{j})-S_{j}\|^{2}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p6.1" class="ltx_p">This is a hard functional constraint. If the lock loss is driven to zero, the field produces exactly the same gating logits for any coordinate within the committed region. Since the same logits produce the same top-<math id="S3.SS5.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> selection and the same softmax weights, and the base parameters <math id="S3.SS5.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{b},B_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{b},B_{b}</annotation></semantics></math> are also constrained by the lock (they cannot change their contribution to locked gating patterns without changing the field output, which is penalized), the effective weight delta for any input that maps to the committed region is preserved exactly.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p7.1" class="ltx_p">The key distinction from regularization-based continual learning methods is that the lock loss operates on the gating function’s outputs at specific points, not on aggregate parameter importance estimates. This means the guarantee is local and precise. The field is free to change its behavior arbitrarily for coordinates outside committed regions.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.6 </span>Sequential Task Learning Protocol</h3>

<div id="S3.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The full multi-task protocol proceeds as follows. On the first task, training proceeds normally with <math id="S3.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{lock}}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>lock</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{lock}}=0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\text{sep}}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mtext>sep</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\text{sep}}=0</annotation></semantics></math>. After convergence, the region is committed. On each subsequent task, training proceeds with the lock loss active for all previously committed regions and the separation loss pushing coordinates away from those regions. After convergence, the new task’s region is committed, and the process repeats.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This protocol ensures that the system’s knowledge grows monotonically. Each committed region represents a frozen capability that cannot be degraded by future training. The coordinate space acts as an address book for capabilities, and the commitment protocol acts as a write-once lock that prevents overwriting.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Model Architecture </h2>

<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Adapter Bank Parameterization</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each target module in the transformer backbone is wrapped with an NIWFLinear layer that contains the adapter bank. For a Mistral-7B model, the target modules span all seven linear projections in each of the 32 transformer layers, specifically the query, key, value, and output projections in the attention block and the gate, up, and down projections in the MLP block. This gives a total of <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32\times 7=224" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>32</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>224</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32\times 7=224</annotation></semantics></math> NIWFLinear modules.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Each NIWFLinear module maintains its own independent bank of <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{b}</annotation></semantics></math> adapter bases. The bases are not shared across modules, allowing each projection to specialize its conditional capacity independently. The total parameter count for the adapter banks is:</p>
<table id="S4.E14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\text{adapt}}=L_{\text{layers}}\cdot\sum_{m\in\text{modules}}N_{b}\cdot r\cdot(d_{\text{in}}^{(m)}+d_{\text{out}}^{(m)})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>adapt</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mtext>layers</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.055em">⋅</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>∈</mo><mtext>modules</mtext></mrow></munder><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mtext>in</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mtext>out</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\text{adapt}}=L_{\text{layers}}\cdot\sum_{m\in\text{modules}}N_{b}\cdot r\cdot(d_{\text{in}}^{(m)}+d_{\text{out}}^{(m)})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For Mistral-7B with <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{b}=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{b}=16</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=8</annotation></semantics></math>, this evaluates to approximately 1.29 GB in 32-bit floating point. With AdamW optimizer states (momentum and variance), the total adapter-related memory is approximately 3.88 GB.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Weight Field Architecture</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The weight field is a three-layer MLP with <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{z}=64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{z}=64</annotation></semantics></math> input dimension, hidden dimension <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{h}=256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>h</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>256</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{h}=256</annotation></semantics></math>, and output dimension <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L\times N_{b}=32\times 16=512" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>32</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>512</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L\times N_{b}=32\times 16=512</annotation></semantics></math> (when not sharing across layers). LayerNorm is applied at the input, and GELU activations are used between layers. The total parameter count of the weight field is approximately 200K, which is negligible compared to the adapter banks and backbone.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">An important design decision is whether to share gating decisions across layers (one set of logits for all layers) or produce per-layer gating. Per-layer gating allows different transformer blocks to activate different base combinations for the same input, which is more expressive. In our experiments, we use per-layer gating unless otherwise specified.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Coordinate Dynamics Architecture</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The coordinate dynamics module consists of a GRUCell with input size <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\text{hidden}}=4096" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>hidden</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>4096</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\text{hidden}}=4096</annotation></semantics></math> (Mistral-7B’s hidden dimension) and hidden size <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{z}=64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>z</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{z}=64</annotation></semantics></math>, followed by LayerNorm, a linear projection, and a <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tanh" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>tanh</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tanh</annotation></semantics></math> activation. The hidden states from the backbone’s final layer are mean-pooled over the sequence dimension to produce the input to the GRU. The GRU’s hidden state is the current coordinate <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tanh" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>tanh</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tanh</annotation></semantics></math> bounding is important for the region commitment protocol. Without it, coordinates could drift to arbitrarily large values during training, making the Gaussian region model a poor fit. With <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tanh" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>tanh</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tanh</annotation></semantics></math>, all coordinates lie within the hypercube <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-1,1]^{64}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mn>64</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-1,1]^{64}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the Gaussian model provides a reasonable approximation to the empirical distribution.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Two-Pass Forward Strategy</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The NIWF forward pass requires knowing the capability coordinate <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> before the backbone’s forward pass (since <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> determines the gating decisions), but <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> depends on the backbone’s hidden states (which are produced during the forward pass). We resolve this circular dependency with a two-pass strategy.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In the first pass, the backbone processes the input with the initial coordinate <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{0}=\mathbf{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>𝟎</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{0}=\mathbf{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, producing hidden states <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{(1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{(1)}</annotation></semantics></math>. These hidden states are mean-pooled and fed to the dynamics module to produce <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{1}=G_{\phi}(z_{0},\bar{h}^{(1)})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{1}=G_{\phi}(z_{0},\bar{h}^{(1)})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In the second pass, the backbone processes the same input with gating decisions derived from <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, producing the final output and loss. The hidden states from the first pass are detached from the computation graph to prevent gradients from flowing back through the backbone during the <math id="S4.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> update step.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p4.1" class="ltx_p">This strategy doubles the number of backbone forward passes during training, but since the backbone is frozen and no gradients flow through it, each pass is relatively cheap. At inference time, the same two-pass strategy is used, adding additional latency compared to the base model. Future work could explore amortized or cached strategies to reduce this overhead.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Experiments</h2>

<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Experimental Setup</h3>

<div id="S5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We validate NIWF on a two-task sequential learning scenario using Mistral-7B-v0.1 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jiang et al., 2023</a>)</cite> as the frozen backbone. The two tasks are:</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Task A (instruction following): We train on 4,000 examples from the Alpaca dataset <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Taori et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, which contains general-purpose instruction-response pairs covering diverse topics including summarization, question answering, creative writing, and factual recall.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Task B (code generation): We train on 4,000 examples from the CodeAlpaca-20k dataset <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chaudhary, 2023</a>)</cite>, which contains code-specific instruction-response pairs covering Python, JavaScript, SQL, and other programming languages.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The training protocol is: (1) Train on Task A until convergence. (2) Commit Task A’s region. (3) Train on Task B with the lock loss active for Task A’s committed region and the separation loss pushing Task B’s coordinates away from Task A’s region. (4) Evaluate on both tasks.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">All experiments use a single NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPU with 24 GB VRAM. The backbone is loaded in bfloat16, and adapter parameters are maintained in float32. Training uses AdamW with a learning rate of <math id="S5.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>, weight decay of 0.01, linear warmup over 5% of steps followed by cosine decay, gradient clipping at 1.0, micro-batch size of 1 with 16 gradient accumulation steps, and a maximum sequence length of 256 tokens.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T1" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 1: </span>NIWF hyperparameters for the Mistral-7B experiments.</figcaption>

<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Memory Analysis</h3>

<figure id="S5.F3" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18628v1/figH_memory_scaling.svg" id="S5.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/173;" width="476" height="173"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 3: </span>Memory and scaling analysis. Left, GPU memory footprint
comparison showing NIWF fits within 24 GB. Center, stored versus
active parameter scaling as base count grows. Right, sequence-level
gating provides 500x memory savings over token-level gating at
sequence length 2048.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A practical concern for NIWF is whether the adapter banks, weight field, and dynamics module fit within the memory constraints of a single GPU alongside the frozen backbone. Table <a href="#S5.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 5.2 Memory Analysis ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Non-Interfering Weight Fields: Treating Model Parameters as a Continuously Extensible Function" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> provides a detailed breakdown.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T2" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 2: </span>GPU memory breakdown for NIWF with Mistral-7B on a 24 GB GPU. The adapter banks, optimizer states, and all auxiliary modules fit comfortably within the available memory, leaving approximately 5 GB of headroom for activations and PyTorch overhead.</figcaption>

<td id="S5.T2.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_tt">Parameters</td>

<tr id="S5.T2.2.6" class="ltx_tr">

</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The key insight enabling this fit is the sequence-level gating strategy described in Equations <a href="#S3.E3" title="In 3.1 Frozen Backbone with Conditional Adapter Banks ‣ 3 Method ‣ Non-Interfering Weight Fields: Treating Model Parameters as a Continuously Extensible Function" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>–<a href="#S3.E5" title="In 3.1 Frozen Backbone with Conditional Adapter Banks ‣ 3 Method ‣ Non-Interfering Weight Fields: Treating Model Parameters as a Continuously Extensible Function" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>. Without this optimization, gathering adapter matrices expanded over the sequence dimension would require <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[B,T,k,d_{\text{out}},r]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[B,T,k,d_{\text{out}},r]</annotation></semantics></math> tensors, consuming approximately 940 MB per MLP module call for <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\text{out}}=14336" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>14336</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\text{out}}=14336</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>256</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=256</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=8</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=8</annotation></semantics></math>. With sequence-level gating, the gather produces <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[B,k,d_{\text{out}},r]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[B,k,d_{\text{out}},r]</annotation></semantics></math> tensors of approximately 1.8 MB, a reduction of over 500x.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.3 </span>Results</h3>

<div id="S5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate NIWF on three metrics. Task A perplexity after Task A training measures the system’s ability to learn the first task. Task A perplexity after Task B training (the forgetting metric) measures whether Task A’s knowledge is preserved. Task B perplexity after Task B training measures the system’s ability to learn new tasks under the locking constraint.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T3" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 3: </span>Perplexity results for the two-task sequential learning protocol. NIWF achieves zero degradation on Task A after training on Task B, compared to catastrophic forgetting baselines. Lower perplexity is better. “Full FT” indicates standard full fine-tuning of all parameters. “LoRA” uses rank-8 adapters. “LoRA Sequential” trains LoRA on Task A, then continues on Task B.</figcaption>
